statement: Data-driven, content-adaptive per-layer budget allocation consistently beats uniform and fixed-pattern (pyramid) allocation under tight KV budgets, and the advantage narrows as the budget approaches full-cache parity. CAKE's preference-prioritized allocation (attention entropy x variance) beats SnapKV/PyramidKV on LongBench at 128L but the margin shrinks at 1024L; LKV's learned global head-wise budget competition further beats heuristic allocators at strict 15% budget and identifies learned budgeting (not selection) as the dominant driver of fidelity. This indicates allocation policy, not just the eviction indicator, is a first-class design axis, and that learned allocation extracts more from a small budget than hand-crafted heuristics can.
